author: Harry
text:
Oedipus wrote: Harry, I drew my flag limit considerably higher than you did. Clearly I haven't grasped this. Would you care to elaborate on why you drew you limit where you did? Thanks for all the work you've put in today.

after the fact its easier to spot them as you understand, so in real time some are cleaner than others. just work with what you have each time. ok, for flag limits two things are important.

as IF said "they signify the end of the momentum" and also we look for them at previous important areas, like obvious SR for example. why? because after the pole, price tries to get back into the area and fails, making a decision and this is our flag limit. so on first return of the price, since the decision has already been made, we can expect a reaction. also, the flag limit area may hold for more tries than the first visit and is valid till broken (but i dont advise anyone to trade it a 2nd time)

after the flag limit is engulfed price is free to travel back to the base of the pole, like in Hotochin's example.

author: Hotochin
text:
Hotochin wrote:

Hey Harry, this might help Oedipus. I want you to make sure I am correct though. Could you look at smaller range candles after big momentum candles as a FL? If you look at the example above I picked the area that the first purple arrow on the left is pointing to with that same logic. I saw some big long green bars then a small green bodied bar.

The obvious follow up to that is I have noticed some people wait for that flag limit to be engulfed as a clue to enter. And I have noticed some people wait for price to move into a level, and then wait for an engulf of the origin of that move before taking a position.

I have another example below. Just look at the FL for now, forget everything else. I have a blue rectangle marked around a FL. Why do some people wait for this FL to get engulfed before entering and others wait for the engulf of the origination of the move that set the FL? See 60min chart below.

Here is the 60min of what price did when it entered the FL. Please ignore that price fell through the FL for a moment. What I am trying to get you to see is up by the red arrow. This was the origination of the move into the FL area. You can see that it was well above the FL itself. Why do some people wait for this area to get engulfed and not just the FL? The reason I ask is because if you look at my original post, the people that waited for the engulf of the FL would have hit the trade just fine. People waiting for the engulf of that first move would have missed the trade entirely as price never came back. I have noticed many times that I trade the engulf of a FL by entering at the origin of that move, price keeps going and stops me out on my entry.

author: Harry
text:
Hotochin, from the flag i like to trade the FTB to the FL, and the break of the flag after price returns to it (after it has filled the pole base).

to trade the engulf of the FL would require a few things - that the further FL point is a reaction to something significant. - and also that it gives me a clear place like an FTR or such to base a trade on.

pedini and sunny do that a lot in their journals with good success btw, so they are more experienced in this matter. not all structures are good for such a trade but they find good ones and they work for them

btw, if you have specific example post it and we can discuss it
